title: Corrected t: how should a per-field-masking-rate model be given t while decoding in a fixed order, to match MD4?
headline: The corrected t fixes a real mismatch, but the model barely reads t
setup: The model fills a team's 84 fields in 84 passes. At each pass it is told t, a number from 0 to 1 that says how much of the team is still hidden. Training and the sampler disagree about what a given t means. This ticket worked out the t that matches training, as the published MD4 paper does, and a later check measured whether the model cares.
alt: At the halfway pass the sampler tells the model t = 0.50, but in training half the team was hidden at t = 0.65. Telling the model the corrected t moved its choices by 0.005 on today's default model and 0.008 on a model trained on the shuffled-only table, both under the bar of 0.01.
terms: A number from 0 to 1 that the model is told: how much of the team is still hidden
One run of the model while it fills a team. There are 84 passes, one field each
One of the 84 values that make a team: for each of six Pokémon its species, ability, item, four moves, Stat Alignment and six Stat Points
In training a field is hidden with chance t raised to a power: 16 for species, 4 for ability and item, 1.5 for moves, 1 otherwise
The t at which training hid as many fields as are still hidden at this pass
How far the model's choices move when told another t: 0 is no change, 1 a complete change. The bar of 0.01 was set before measuring

frames.title: 1. Halfway through sampling: 42 of 84 fields filled
frames.takes: The sampler fills species first, then abilities and items, then moves. Here half the team is still hidden.
frames.measured: The sampler tells the model t = 0.50.

frames.title: 2. What t = 0.50 meant in training
frames.takes: Training almost never hid a species at t = 0.50, so it hid less than half the team.
frames.measured: 36% of the team hidden, 30 of 84 fields. Half was hidden at t = 0.65.

frames.title: 3. Today's t against the corrected t
frames.takes: The corrected t sits above today's t at every pass.
frames.measured: 0.65 against 0.50 at the halfway pass, and 0.97 against 0.93 after six fields.

frames.title: 4. Does the model care which t it is told?
frames.takes: The model barely reads t, so the fix changes almost nothing.
frames.measured: Largest shift 0.005 on today's default model, and 0.008 on a model trained on the shuffled-only table.
